deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a space or topos X with a stratification indexed by a poset I. The strata are X_i, and for a crible (sieve, i.e. down-closed subset) I' of I, X_{I'} is the closed union of the corresponding strata. The stratified space has 'elementary' pieces: the strata X_i^* and, for each pair i<j (in this text, j a successor of i), a tubular piece V_{ij} and a deleted tubular piece V_{ij}^*. Together these form a diagram indexed by a category Ĩ built from I (objects i and pairs i<j, with arrows V_{ij}^* -> X_j^* and V_{ij}^* -> V_{ij} -> X_i^*). This diagram is meant to encode the stratified homotopy type, by gluing along the deleted neighbourhoods.

On this page Grothendieck makes three observations.

(1) Empty strata. Let I_0 = {i : X_i = ∅}. I_0 is a crible: by the frontier condition, j ≤ i implies X_j ⊂ closure(X_i), so if X_i is empty then X_j is empty too. For i in I_0 all elementary spaces attached to i vanish. So, discarding empty spaces, the Ĩ-diagram of X is obtained by restricting to I∖I_0. More generally one may restrict to I∖I'_0 for any crible I'_0 ⊂ I_0, and the resulting index category is a full subcategory of Ĩ.

(2) Pairs of cribles. Given cribles I'' ⊂ I' ⊂ I, one gets closed subspaces X_{I''} ⊂ X_{I'}. Set U_{I',I''} := X_{I'} ∖ X_{I''}, which is open in X_{I'} and locally closed in X. U_{I',I''} carries an induced stratification indexed by the locally closed (convex) subposet I'∖I''. Its strata are X_{i'} ∖ (X_{i'} ∩ X_{I''}).

(3) Elementary topoi of the piece. The elementary topoi of U_{I',I''} are the X_{i'}^* for i' ∈ I'∖I'', together with relative tubular pieces V^*_{i'j',X'} and V_{i'j',X'}. These are the old tubular pieces cut down to the open piece.

The next page notes that the comparison maps V_{i'j',X'} -> V_{i'j'} need not be homotopy equivalences, so he postpones comparing constructions on X_{I'} and on U_{I',I''}.

Purpose: functoriality of the 'elementary diagram' description of a stratified space/topos under passage to closed unions of strata and to locally closed pieces. This is groundwork for the subsequent constructions V^{I'''}_{I',I''} (section c on the next page).
errors: Slip in the manuscript: 'où I'_0 ⊂ I'_0' should read 'I'_0 ⊂ I_0'.

The page tacitly suggests the elementary pieces of U_{I',I''} are the restrictions of those of X. The next page itself admits that the comparison maps between the relative tubular pieces and the original ones need not be homotopy equivalences. So the compatibility is not established here.

ideas.what: Set of indices of empty strata forms a sieve, and the stratification diagram can be restricted to its complement
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of a poset-stratification to a cosieve / refinement removing empty strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (stratified spaces over posets, e.g. Lurie Higher Algebra App. A)

ideas.what: Locally closed piece X_{I'}∖X_{I''} stratified by the convex subposet I'∖I''
ideas.modern_name: Induced stratification over a locally closed / convex subposet

ideas.what: Encoding a stratified space by a diagram of strata and (deleted) tubular neighbourhoods over a category Ĩ built from I
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy links / exit-path decomposition; 'dévissage' of stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopically stratified sets, 1988); Lurie; Douteau–Waas; Grothendieck's Esquisse §5 sketches the program
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 (dévissage of stratified structures), in programmatic form only

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping on restricting a poset-indexed stratification to sieves and locally closed pieces. The only non-trivial point, whether the relative tubular pieces are homotopy equivalent to the originals, is raised but explicitly left open. That issue is well understood today via homotopy links.
transcription_corrections: 'où I'_0 ⊂ I'_0' should be read as 'où I'_0 ⊂ I_0 est un crible'.
The last line uses V (not U): 'des V^*_{i'j',X'}, V_{i'j',X'}', consistent with the next page.
Line 4 likely reads 'V_{ij}^* = V_{ij} = ∅' rather than U.
'C'est une crible' should be 'C'est un crible' (Grothendieck uses masculine).
